display_name: John the Faster, of the Cave

names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Δεκεμβρίου, «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Νηστευτής «ὁ ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ»», with the rank word left off. The by-names «ο Νηστευτής» and «ὁ ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ» are left off the stored form.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru’s line for 7 декабря ст. ст., «Иоанн Печерский, постник», with the by-name «постник», the Faster, left off as the rank-like word it stands in for here; the calendar prints it after a comma as it prints a grade. The line on the day page itself gives the name in the genitive.

feast.note: His life page lists one other day, «28 сентября (Печер.(Б))», the synaxis of the venerable fathers of the Near Caves of Kyiv, where he is buried. One row per church is the schema, so that day is recorded here and he does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 декабря ст. ст. — «Прп. Иоанна, постника Печерского (XII).»

attestations.note: The same man and the same menologion day. The Greek entry this folder was made from is «Ιωάννης ὁ Νηστευτὴς ὁ ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ», John the Faster who is in the Cave, whom that page calls a Russian venerable and of whose life it says it has no details; «Печерский» is that Σπήλαιον — the Caves of Kyiv — and «постник» is the Νηστευτής. The folder's own life already sets him apart from the John the Faster who was patriarch of Constantinople, and this calendar keeps the two apart in the same way. THE JULIAN 29 ДЕКАБРЯ IS A DIFFERENT JOHN, AND NO SECOND ROW IS MADE. Read 13 October 2026. The line is «Прпп. Марка гробокопателя, Феофила и Иоанна Печерских (XI-XII).» and the two lives behind it are life3195, the Paterikon account of the three, and life6622, the short notice of the pair. What settles it is not the lives — neither of them names a day or an epithet this folder carries — but **the calendar's own name index, which keeps these men apart by design and in adjacent entries, and lists for each the days he is kept on.** The name link behind that Иоанн is name page **1002, «Преподобный Иоанн Печерский»**, with no by-name at all, and it heads «Дни памяти: 28 сентября (Печер.(Б)) , 29 декабря» — **7 декабря, this folder's day, is not among them.** This folder's man stands behind name page **1003, «Иоанн Печерский, постник»**, kept on 7 декабря. The index holds a third of the name as well: **1000, «Иоанн Печерский, Киевский, отрок»**, the boy of the Julian 12 июля whom this corpus keeps as `john-son-of-theodore-the-varangian`. Three consecutive-ish entries, three days, three men, and none of the three name pages lists another's day. The centuries part too: the 29 декабря line closes «(XI-XII)» and life6622 has the pair in «конце XI - начале XII вв.», where this folder holds «(XII)» off its line and off life6624. And the dossier is a different man's: the John of 29 декабря is the younger of two brother-monks who shared one grave, who died while his elder brother was away on the monastery's business, and who in death obeyed his brother still and moved over in the coffin to give him the elder's place. Nothing in it is a faster, and **neither life calls him «постник»** — the by-name this folder's whole Greek and Russian identification rests on. BOTH PAIRS LIE IN THE SAME CAVES AND SHARE THE SAME SYNAXIS, WHICH IS WHY THEY READ ALIKE AND IS NEITHER A RELATION NOR AN IDENTITY: every one of these men is kept in the 28 сентября commemoration of the venerable of the Near (Antoniev) caves, and sharing a day is not a relation, the same way a dedication is not. NO FOLDER WAS MADE for Theophilus the Weeper, for his brother John, or for Mark the Gravedigger: a new folder is a different operation from this one, and the 29 декабря line is left for whoever reads that day. NOT CHECKED: no Paterikon edition outside days.pravoslavie.ru was consulted, and the 28 сентября synaxis page was not opened to see whether it numbers the two Theophiluses and the two Johns separately — the name index already does.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Νηστευτής «ὁ ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ»»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and its whole content is «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Ρώσου Οσίου» — we have no details of the Russian venerable's life. The corpus keeps `john-the-faster-patriarch-of-constantinople`, «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Νηστευτής, Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης», on 2 September in all four calendars; that is a patriarch and not a Russian ascetic of a cave, a different entry on the same calendar and therefore a different commemoration. The by-name «ὁ ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ» is the same formula the corpus's `paul-the-obedient-of-the-caves` carries, and the display name here follows that folder's English. No year, so no `dates` object. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (2 October 2026).

death.note: The century the day line closes with for 7 декабря ст. ст., «(XII)», and the century its life page gives: «Подвизался в Киево-Печерском монастыре в XII веке и погребен в Ближних пещерах». The folder held no date at all: saint.gr said outright that it had no details of his life. Read 13 October 2026.
